mainTopic: The amount of קלף and דוכסוסטוס for carrying on שבת, and רב's ruling on which hide may be used for תפילין and מזוזה
overview: The גמרא starts with the משנה's rule that carrying קלף on שבת makes you liable once there is enough to write the shortest פרשה of תפילין. A ברייתא seems to say 'enough to write a מזוזה.' The גמרא settles this by reading the ברייתא as giving a separate amount for each material: a מזוזה for דוכסוסטוס, and שמע ישראל for קלף. Then רב rules that דוכסוסטוס is like קלף, so תפילין may be written on it. The גמרא challenges רב several times. It answers that the sources describe the ideal way (למצוה), or speak about a מזוזה, or reflect a מחלוקת תנאים. Proposed proofs for רב, from תנא דבי מנשה and from worn-out תפילין, are each rejected. Since רבי מאיר wrote a מזוזה on קלף, the גמרא finally rereads רב to mean that קלף, like דוכסוסטוס, is valid for a מזוזה. The amud ends by quoting the next line of the משנה, about ink.

steps.title: The משנה's amount for parchment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that for קלף, the amount that makes you liable for carrying is enough to write a short פרשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Parchment: enough to write a short passage on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from our משנה about the minimum size of קלף that makes a person liable for carrying it on שבת. This sets up the contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each object has its own minimum amount (שיעור) for liability for הוצאה. For קלף, the amount is set by its main use: enough space to write the shortest פרשה of תפילין, which is שמע ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: Parchment; one of the layers of a split animal hide
A short Torah passage (here, the shortest one in תפילין)
Enough to write

phrases.english: Parchment: enough to write on it
a short passage.
phrases.notes: The full משנה adds: 'שבתפילין, שהיא שמע ישראל' (in the תפילין, which is שמע ישראל).

steps.triggerLanguage: קְלָף כְּדֵי לִכְתּוֹב עָלָיו פָּרָשָׁה קְטַנָּה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying קלף makes you liable once it is big enough to write the shortest פרשה of תפילין.

steps.title: A ברייתא gives a different amount
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that קלף and דוכסוסטוס need enough to write a whole מזוזה, which is bigger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they contrasted it: קלף and דוכסוסטוס: enough to write a מזוזה on it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with the משנה about how much קלף you need to be liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזוזה holds two פרשיות (שמע and והיה אם שמוע), so it needs more space than the shortest פרשה of תפילין. That means the two sources give two different minimums for the same material.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contrasted it: introduces a contradicting source
The other layer of a split hide (the partner of קלף)
A מזוזה scroll, with the passages שמע and והיה אם שמוע

phrases.english: And they raised a contradiction:
Parchment and dokhsostos:
enough to write a mezuzah on it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contradicts the amount in the משנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מזוזה is longer than one short פרשה, so the two sources give different minimums.

steps.title: 'Mezuzah' means the mezuzah passage inside tefillin
steps.stepSummary: The word 'מזוזה' in the ברייתא means the מזוזה-passage that is also found in תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'מזוזה'? The מזוזה that is in the תפילין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא is not talking about a whole מזוזה scroll. It means the passage of the מזוזה that also appears in תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמע is a passage found in both a מזוזה and תפילין. If 'מזוזה' here just means that one passage, then the ברייתא and the משנה are giving the same amount.

keyTerms.meaning: What is (asking what a word means)
That is in the תפילין

phrases.english: What is meant by 'mezuzah'?
The mezuzah passage that is in the tefillin.

steps.terutzMaskana: 'מזוזה' means the מזוזה passage inside תפילין, so the amount matches the משנה.

steps.title: Are tefillin ever called 'mezuzah'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether the passages in תפילין are ever called 'מזוזה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do they call תפילין 'מזוזה'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer by asking whether this way of speaking ever actually appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer only works if 'מזוזה' is a known name for the passages in תפילין. Without proof, the reading looks forced.

keyTerms.meaning: And do they call them

phrases.english: And do they call tefillin 'mezuzah'?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The term is never used that way, so the reading seems unlikely.

steps.title: Proof: רבי זכאי calls the tefillin passages 'mezuzah'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא about טומאת ידיים uses 'the מזוזה itself' to mean the parchment inside תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, as it was taught: תפילין straps attached to the תפילין make the hands impure; on their own they do not. רבי שמעון בן יהודה says in the name of רבי שמעון: One who touches the strap is pure until he touches the box. רבי זכאי says in his name: Pure until he touches the מזוזה itself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers 'yes' and proves it from a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, רבי זכאי calls the written passages inside תפילין 'the מזוזה itself.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Holy writings make the hands impure (טומאת ידיים), and the ברייתא asks which parts of תפילין do this. רבי זכאי says you are pure until you touch 'the מזוזה itself', which here clearly means the scroll inside the תפילין. So the name is used, and the answer in step 3 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Straps
Make the hands impure (a rabbinic rule about holy writings)
The box of the תפילין
Ritually pure

phrases.english: Yes, as it was taught:
Tefillin straps together with the tefillin
make the hands impure;
on their own,
they do not make the hands impure.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Shimon:
One who touches the strap is pure,
until he touches the box.
Rabbi Zakkai says in his name:
He is pure until he touches the mezuzah itself.
phrases.notes: 'מזוזה' here means the parchment passages inside the תפילין.

steps.raayaObject: That the passages in תפילין are called 'מזוזה'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about טומאת ידיים, opinion of רבי זכאי

steps.title: The ברייתא's own second half shows it means a real mezuzah
steps.stepSummary: The same ברייתא later says קלף = the short פרשה of שמע, so its first half must mean a full מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But since the latter clause teaches 'קלף: enough to write the short passage in תפילין, which is שמע ישראל,' it follows that the first clause deals with an actual מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer again. The ברייתא's own later clause already covers the תפילין passage, so the first clause must mean something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both clauses meant the same short passage, the ברייתא would be repeating itself. So the first clause, 'מזוזה', must mean a real מזוזה scroll, and the contradiction with the משנה comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: The later clause
The first clause
It follows that / by inference
We are dealing with

phrases.english: But since the latter clause teaches:
'Parchment: enough to write on it
the short passage in the tefillin,
which is Shema Yisrael',
it follows that in the first clause
we are dealing with an actual mezuzah!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא would be repeating itself, so 'מזוזה' in the first clause must mean a full מזוזה.

steps.title: Each material gets its own amount
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives a separate amount for each material: דוכסוסטוס = a מזוזה, קלף = שמע ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it teaches: קלף and דוכסוסטוס, what is their amount? דוכסוסטוס: enough to write a מזוזה on it. קלף: enough to write on it the short passage in תפילין, which is שמע ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as one question with two answers, one answer for each material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first clause, 'מזוזה', is about דוכסוסטוס, which is used for writing a מזוזה. קלף is used for תפילין, so its amount is the short passage, just like the משנה says. Now there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches (rereading the source)
Their minimum amount

steps.whatToRemember: The amount follows how each material is normally used: דוכסוסטוס is for a מזוזה, and קלף is for תפילין.

phrases.english: This is what it teaches:
Parchment and dokhsostos, how much is their amount?
Dokhsostos: enough to write a mezuzah on it.
Parchment: enough to write on it
the short passage in tefillin, which is Shema Yisrael.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the structure of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both materials share one amount, a מזוזה.
steps.terutzMaskana: דוכסוסטוס = a מזוזה; קלף = שמע ישראל, which matches the משנה.

steps.title: רב: dokhsostos is like parchment for tefillin
steps.stepSummary: רב rules that תפילין may be written on דוכסוסטוס, just as on קלף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: דוכסוסטוס is like קלף. Just as one writes תפילין on קלף, so too one writes תפילין on דוכסוסטוס.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב says the two hide layers are equal for writing תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now each material had its usual job. רב says this is not a strict rule: תפילין written on דוכסוסטוס are also kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: It is just like
One may write

phrases.english: Rav said:
Dokhsostos is like parchment.
Just as one writes tefillin on parchment,
so too one writes tefillin on dokhsostos.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב: דּוּכְסוּסְטוֹס הֲרֵי הוּא כִּקְלָף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפילין written on דוכסוסטוס are kosher, like those written on קלף.

steps.title: The משנה mentions only parchment for tefillin
steps.stepSummary: The משנה connects תפילין to קלף only, which suggests דוכסוסטוס is not allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: קלף, enough to write the short passage in תפילין, which is שמע ישראל. קלף, yes; דוכסוסטוס, no?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב from the משנה, which links תפילין only to קלף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument comes from what the משנה leaves out. If דוכסוסטוס were also fine for תפילין, the משנה should have mentioned it too.

keyTerms.meaning: We learned (in a משנה)
Yes ... no (an inference from what is left out)

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: קְלָף כְּדֵי לִכְתּוֹב פָּרָשָׁה קְטַנָּה שֶׁבַּתְּפִילִּין
phrases.english: We learned: Parchment, enough to write the short passage in tefillin,
which is Shema Yisrael.
Parchment, yes; dokhsostos, no?!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה names only קלף for תפילין, which implies דוכסוסטוס is not allowed.

steps.title: The משנה describes the best way
steps.stepSummary: קלף is the preferred material (למצוה), but דוכסוסטוס still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the מצוה [in its best form].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה names the ideal material, not the only kosher one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a difference between 'best practice' and 'required.' Writing on קלף is the best way, but writing on דוכסוסטוס is still kosher, so רב is not contradicted.

keyTerms.meaning: The best, preferred way to do the מצוה (not required)

steps.confusionAlert: 'למצוה' does NOT mean 'required.' It means the ideal way. If you do it differently, it is still kosher.

phrases.english: For the optimal מצוה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Ideal practice vs. what is required
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only קלף is kosher for תפילין.
steps.terutzMaskana: קלף is ideal; דוכסוסטוס is still kosher.

steps.title: A הלכה למשה מסיני assigns tefillin to parchment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says it is a הלכה למשה מסיני that תפילין go on קלף and מזוזה on דוכסוסטוס, each on a set side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come hear: It is a הלכה למשה מסיני: תפילין on קלף and מזוזה on דוכסוסטוס. קלף on the flesh side, דוכסוסטוס on the hair side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger source against רב: a law from Sinai that matches each item to a material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הלכה למשה מסיני sounds like a firm requirement, not just a preference. It also says which side of the hide to write on, so the matching seems exact and binding.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (introduces a proof or challenge)
A law given orally to משה at Sinai
On the side that faced the flesh
On the side that faced the hair

phrases.english: Come and hear:
It is a halakha to Moshe from Sinai:
tefillin on parchment
and mezuzah on dokhsostos.
Parchment: on the flesh side;
dokhsostos: on the hair side.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law from Sinai assigns תפילין to קלף, which seems to rule out דוכסוסטוס.

steps.title: This too describes the best way
steps.stepSummary: The same answer: the הלכה למשה מסיני gives the ideal pairing.
steps.simpleTranslation: For the מצוה [in its best form].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer again: this source also describes the preferred way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a הלכה למשה מסיני can set the ideal way without making other ways invalid. So רב still stands.

phrases.english: For the optimal מצוה.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Ideal practice vs. what is required
steps.terutzMaskana: The Sinai pairing is the ideal, not a requirement for תפילין.

steps.title: 'If he deviated, it is invalid'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that changing from the set pairing makes it invalid, so it is not just a preference.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: If he deviated, it is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'למצוה' answer: a ברייתא says that changing the material makes it פסול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If changing makes it פסול, then the pairing is required, not just ideal. That would go against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: He deviated / changed (from the set way)
Invalid

phrases.english: But it was taught: If he deviated, it is invalid!

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Changing invalidates, so the pairing is required.

steps.title: That rule is about a mezuzah
steps.stepSummary: The invalidation applies to a מזוזה, not to תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: On a mezuzah.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'deviating is invalid' is said only about a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזוזה written on the wrong material is פסול. תפילין, however, may be on either material, as רב says. So the strictness only applies to מזוזה.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding a מזוזה

phrases.english: It refers to a mezuzah.

steps.terutzMaskana: Only a מזוזה is invalidated by deviating.

steps.title: 'Deviated in this or that' includes tefillin
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא says that deviating 'in this and in that' is invalid, which seems to include תפילין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: If he deviated in this or in that, it is invalid!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to talk about both items, so the 'only מזוזה' answer seems not to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'This and that' sounds like תפילין and מזוזה. If so, deviating for תפילין would also be פסול, against רב.

keyTerms.meaning: In this and in that

phrases.english: But it was taught: If he deviated in this or in that, it is invalid!

steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that the invalidation is only about מזוזה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'This and that' seems to cover both תפילין and מזוזה.

steps.title: Both cases are about a mezuzah
steps.stepSummary: 'This and that' means two ways of writing a מזוזה wrong: on קלף on the hair side, or on דוכסוסטוס on the flesh side.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both this and that refer to a מזוזה: where he wrote it on קלף on the hair side, or on דוכסוסטוס on the flesh side.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that 'this and that' are two kinds of mistakes, both in a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are writing a מזוזה on the wrong side of either material. Both are about מזוזה, so תפילין are not affected and רב still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that (both)
Or alternatively

phrases.english: Both this and that refer to a mezuzah,
and this is where he wrote it on parchment on the hair side,
or on dokhsostos on the flesh side.

steps.terutzMaskana: 'This and that' = two wrong-side cases for a מזוזה.

steps.title: A second answer: it is a dispute of תנאים
steps.stepSummary: Another approach: whether deviating in both is פסול is a מחלוקת תנאים, and רבי אחא rules it kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or if you want, say: 'deviated in this or that' is a dispute of תנאים. As it was taught: If he deviated in this or that, it is invalid. רבי אחא validates it in the name of רבי אחי בר חנינא, and some say in the name of רבי יעקב son of רבי חנינא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second answer. The ברייתא really does mean תפילין and מזוזה, but other תנאים disagree with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of reinterpreting the ברייתא, this answer accepts its plain meaning. It shows that רבי אחא holds deviating is kosher, so רב can follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: Or if you wish, say (a second answer)
It is a dispute between תנאים
Rules it valid
And some say (a different chain of names)

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
'deviated in this or that' is a dispute of Tannaim.
As it was taught: If he deviated in this or that, it is invalid.
Rabbi Acha validates it
in the name of Rabbi Achai bar Chanina,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: and some say in the name of Rabbi Yaakov son of Rabbi Chanina.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing it is a dispute (מחלוקת תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Deviating with תפילין is פסול according to everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a dispute; רב follows רבי אחא, who rules it kosher.

steps.title: רב פפא: רב follows תנא דבי מנשה
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says רב follows תנא דבי מנשה, who rules that writing 'it' on קלף, גויל, or דוכסוסטוס is kosher, but on paper or cloth is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: רב spoke according to the Tanna of the school of Menashe. As the school of Menashe taught: If he wrote it on paper or on cloth, it is invalid; on parchment, on gevil, or on dokhsostos, it is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a different source for רב's view: a תנא who treats all three hide materials as kosher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: תנא דבי מנשה rules that writing on any real hide (קלף, גויל, or דוכסוסטוס) is kosher, and only paper or cloth are פסול. רב פפא reads this as being about תפילין, which would allow תפילין on דוכסוסטוס, as רב said. The next step spells out why it must be תפילין, and step 20 rejects that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא of the school of מנשה
Paper
A cloth
A full, unsplit hide, processed with gallnuts
Valid

steps.whatToRemember: So far, רב's view is defended: the sources that pair תפילין with קלף describe the ideal (למצוה) or are about a מזוזה, and רבי אחא supports him. The proof from תנא דבי מנשה is tested in the next steps, and step 20 rejects it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It tries to give רב a source among the תנאים. Steps 19–20 test this proof and reject it.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Rav spoke according to the Tanna of the school of Menashe.
As the school of Menashe taught:

phrases.aramaic: כְּתָבָהּ עַל הַנְּיָיר וְעַל הַמַּטְלֵית — פְּסוּלָה.
phrases.english: If he wrote it on paper or on cloth, it is invalid.

phrases.aramaic: עַל הַקְּלָף וְעַל הַגְּוִיל וְעַל דּוּכְסוּסְטוֹס — כְּשֵׁרָה.
phrases.english: On parchment, on gevil, or on dokhsostos, it is valid.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: רַב דְּאָמַר כְּתַנָּא דְבֵי מְנַשֶּׁה
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finding a source in a תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב has no support among the תנאים.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב follows תנא דבי מנשה, for whom all hide materials are kosher.

steps.title: Which item does the ברייתא mean: מזוזה or תפילין?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what object the ברייתא is describing. It argues it cannot be a מזוזה, so it must be תפילין, which would support רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If he wrote it.' Wrote what? If you say a מזוזה, do we write a מזוזה on קלף? So isn't it talking about תפילין?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא looks at a ברייתא that allows writing on several materials, including דוכסוסטוס, and asks what is being written. It reasons step by step that the ברייתא must be about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא also allows קלף. The גמרא assumes a מזוזה is never written on קלף, so it rules out מזוזה. That leaves תפילין, which would mean תפילין can be written on דוכסוסטוס, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: He wrote it (the 'it' is unclear, which is what the גמרא asks about)
If you say (proposes an option in order to reject it)
Do we write? (a question that expects the answer 'no')
Rather, isn't it...? (introduces the conclusion the speaker wants)

phrases.english: 'He wrote it': wrote what?
If you say a mezuza,
do we write a mezuza on klaf?
Rather, is it not tefillin?
phrases.notes: If so, the ברייתא allows writing tefillin on דוכסוסטוס, which supports רב.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains רב פפא's proof in step 18: by elimination, the דבי מנשה ברייתא must be about תפילין.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that תפילין may be written on דוכסוסטוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that allows writing on קלף, גויל, and דוכסוסטוס, which (by elimination) seems to be about תפילין

steps.title: The ברייתא is about a ספר תורה
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: תפילין are not written on גויל either, so the ברייתא must be about a ספר תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your own logic, do we write תפילין on גויל?! Rather, that ברייתא was taught about a ספר תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the same argument around. The ברייתא also allows גויל, which is never used for תפילין, so it cannot be about תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ruling out by elimination works against תפילין just as well as against מזוזה. The only item that fits every material on the list is a ספר תורה, so the ברייתא offers no support for רב.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning (turns the questioner's logic back on him)
Thick, whole hide that has not been split, the usual material for a ספר תורה
A Torah scroll

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
do we write tefillin on gevil?!
Rather, when that [baraita] was taught,
it was about a Torah scroll.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The identification of the ברייתא's subject as תפילין
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ruling-out logic fails, because גויל does not fit תפילין. The ברייתא fits only a ספר תורה.

steps.title: A second proof for רב from worn-out תפילין
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says worn-out תפילין may not be made into a מזוזה because one may not lower holiness. That suggests that, without this rule, it would be allowed, so the תפילין must have been written on דוכסוסטוס, the מזוזה material.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this supports רב: Similarly, worn-out תפילין and a worn-out ספר תורה may not be made into a מזוזה, because we do not lower something from greater holiness to lesser holiness. So the only reason is lowering holiness. If lowering were allowed, one could make a מזוזה from them. And what were those תפילין written on? Wasn't it דוכסוסטוס!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another ברייתא to support רב. It reads into the reason the ברייתא gives in order to show that תפילין are written on דוכסוסטוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא blocks the switch only because of holiness. That implies the material itself would work for a מזוזה. Since a מזוזה is written on דוכסוסטוס, the תפילין must also have been on דוכסוסטוס, just as רב said.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him
That became worn out
We do not lower (something to a lesser level)
Greater holiness / lesser holiness
The reason is X; this implies that otherwise... (an inference from a stated reason)
The inner layer of a split hide

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
Similarly, tefillin that wore out
and a Torah scroll that wore out:
one may not make a mezuza from them,
because one does not lower
from greater holiness to lesser holiness.
The reason is that one does not lower;
but if one did lower, one would make [a mezuza].
On what is it written?
Is it not written on dukhsustus!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first proof failed, this offers a different proof for רב.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that תפילין may be written on דוכסוסטוס
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about worn-out תפילין and the inference drawn from its stated reason

steps.title: Those תפילין were written on קלף
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected: the תפילין in that ברייתא were written on קלף.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It was written on קלף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא blocks the second proof. The תפילין in the case could have been on ordinary קלף, not דוכסוסטוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תפילין were on קלף, the ברייתא says nothing about דוכסוסטוס for תפילין. This answer, however, raises a new problem, which the next step asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: One of the two layers of a split hide (which layer is debated), the standard material for תפילין

phrases.english: No, it is written on klaf.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The assumption that those תפילין were on דוכסוסטוס
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Nothing forces that assumption. The תפילין could have been on קלף.

steps.title: Can a מזוזה be written on קלף?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the rejection: if the תפילין were on קלף, how could the ברייתא even consider making them into a מזוזה?
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we write a מזוזה on קלף?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer just given. A מזוזה is normally written on דוכסוסטוס, so תפילין on קלף should not qualify for a מזוזה anyway.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא implies that the only obstacle is lowering holiness. If קלף were invalid for a מזוזה, there would already be a second, more basic obstacle, so the answer 'on קלף' seems to fail.

phrases.english: But do we write a mezuza on klaf?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the תפילין in the ברייתא were written on קלף
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A מזוזה is not written on קלף. So the material would already block the switch, yet the ברייתא names only holiness as the reason.

steps.title: רבי מאיר wrote a מזוזה on קלף
steps.stepSummary: Yes, a מזוזה may be written on קלף. A ברייתא reports that רבי מאיר did so because it lasts longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes. A ברייתא teaches: if he wrote it on קלף, on paper, or on cloth, it is invalid. רבי שמעון בן אלעזר said: רבי מאיר used to write it on קלף, because it lasts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that, at least according to רבי מאיר, a מזוזה may be written on קלף. It proves this from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא invalidates a מזוזה on קלף, but רבי מאיר wrote his on קלף. So according to him, תפילין on קלף could become a מזוזה if not for the holiness rule. The ברייתא about worn-out תפילין therefore fits קלף perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes
And it was taught in a ברייתא
Paper
A piece of cloth
It is preserved; it lasts

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's opening line says קלף is invalid for a מזוזה. The proof comes only from רבי מאיר's practice, which disagrees with that opening line.

phrases.english: Yes, as it was taught:
If one wrote it on klaf,
on paper, or on cloth, it is invalid.
Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר הָיָה כּוֹתְבָהּ עַל הַקְּלָף,
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir would write it on klaf,
because it is preserved.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a supporting source: a תנא (רבי מאיר) who allows a מזוזה on קלף
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A מזוזה can never be written on קלף.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי מאיר, a מזוזה may be written on קלף, so the ברייתא about worn-out תפילין can refer to תפילין on קלף.

steps.title: רב's statement is reread as being about מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: Now רב is reread: not 'דוכסוסטוס is like קלף' for תפילין, but 'קלף is like דוכסוסטוס' for a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have reached this point, for רב as well, do not say 'דוכסוסטוס is like קלף.' Rather, say 'קלף is like דוכסוסטוס': just as a מזוזה may be written on דוכסוסטוס, so too a מזוזה may be written on קלף.
steps.whatsHappening: Since we now see that a מזוזה can be written on קלף, the גמרא reinterprets רב's original statement. It makes רב's statement about a מזוזה instead of תפילין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this step, רב seemed to extend דוכסוסטוס to תפילין. Now רב is read as extending קלף to a מזוזה, following רבי מאיר. This removes the difficulty with the rule that תפילין are written on קלף.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this (introduces a new understanding)
Do not say X; rather, say Y (rewording a statement)
It is just like; it has the same status as

steps.whatToRemember: In the end, רב means that a מזוזה may be written on קלף just as on דוכסוסטוס, following רבי מאיר. רב does not mean that תפילין may be written on דוכסוסטוס.
steps.whyThisMatters: It settles the long back-and-forth about רב's statement by turning it around so that it no longer conflicts with the rule that תפילין are written on קלף.

phrases.english: Now that you have arrived at this,
for Rav as well, do not say
'dukhsustus is like klaf,'

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: קְלָף הֲרֵי הוּא כְּדוּכְסוּסְטוֹס,
phrases.english: rather say: 'klaf is like dukhsustus':
just as on dukhsustus one writes a mezuza,
so too on klaf one writes a mezuza.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, לְרַב נָמֵי לָא תֵּימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי מאיר's view from step 24 to reread רב.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב's statement means that קלף, like דוכסוסטוס, is valid for a מזוזה.

steps.title: משנה: the measure for ink
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one is liable for carrying out enough ink to write.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ink: enough to write.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next item in the משנה, the minimum amount of ink that makes one liable for carrying it out on שבת. This line sets up a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. According to the משנה, the amount is enough ink to write two letters.

keyTerms.meaning: Ink
Enough to write (two letters)

phrases.english: Ink: enough to write.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. The full measure there is enough to write two letters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, returning to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Carrying out enough ink to write two letters makes one liable on שבת.
